finding.claim: Ruby authorizer exception unwinds through sqlite3_prepare via unprotected rb_funcall, skipping SQLite mutex release and parser cleanup
finding.source: SQL text supplies identifiers a-d (database.c:734-737) that reach the app authorizer

trace.note: rb_sqlite3_auth calls authorizer with rb_funcall, no rb_protect

finding.guards_checked: UDFs and aggregators use rb_protect (database.c:581, aggregator.c:41-47); authorizer path does not. Impact depends on app authorizer raising. Not verified by running.

finding.claim: Collation comparator exception unwinds through sqlite3_step via unprotected rb_funcall, leaving SQLite state inconsistent
finding.source: Stored row text compared under a collation whose Ruby comparator raises on some value
finding.sink: rb_funcall non-local exit inside SQLite sort during sqlite3_step

trace.note: rb_comparator_func calls compare with rb_funcall, no rb_protect
NUM2INT on comparator result, raises TypeError for non-integer

finding.guards_checked: rb_errinfo re-raise in step (statement.c:143-150) only covers protected calls; no rb_protect on comparator path. Not verified by running.

finding.claim: Authorizer return mapping fails open: any non-Integer, non-boolean return becomes SQLITE_IGNORE instead of SQLITE_DENY
finding.source: App authorizer returns nil or another object on some branch
finding.sink: SQLITE_IGNORE permits the action (reads yield NULL, writes silently skipped)
finding.guards_checked: Explicit true/false/integer returns handled correctly. Depends on app authorizer code.

finding.claim: On 64-bit builds, Ruby Integers in [2^62, 2^63) returned from user-defined SQL functions are converted to double and lose low bits
finding.source: Integer computed by a define_function block from data derived from attacker input
finding.sink: sqlite3_result_double at database.c:521 feeding a WHERE or ownership comparison in SQL

trace.note: bignum-to-int64 block compiled out when SIZEOF_LONG >= 8

finding.guards_checked: Bind path handles int64-range bignums correctly (statement.c:285-290). Bind path out-of-range bignums also become doubles (statement.c:292-294), e.g. -2^63-1 can match stored -2^63. Requires app using 63-bit UDF outputs for security checks.

finding.claim: UTF-16 path helper appends NUL terminator to the caller's own string object, mutating it
finding.source: Caller passes a UTF-16 path string to open16
finding.sink: rb_str_buf_cat on the caller's str object at database.c:189, reached from database.c:1048

trace.note: NUL check performed on a dup
appends to original str, not the dup

finding.guards_checked: Embedded-NUL check runs on dup (lines 184-187). Frozen string raises FrozenError. Second open with same object fails the NUL check.

finding.claim: Ruby string lengths cast to int without range check, truncating or negating lengths of 2 GiB or more
finding.source: Caller-supplied SQL or bound value of 2 GiB or more
finding.sink: (int)RSTRING_LEN passed to sqlite3_prepare_v2 and sqlite3_bind_* (also statement.c:257, 268, 279 and database.c:530, 537)
finding.guards_checked: Ruby strings are NUL-terminated, so truncation yields data corruption rather than out-of-bounds read. Practically unreachable.
